findings.title: STT extra body never populated; attribution untested
findings.problem: get_litellm_stt_client returns dict(request_params.get('model_kwargs') or {}) as the extra body, documented as carrying the customer id as the OpenAI 'user' field. Grep of src/codemie/enterprise/litellm shows nothing writes 'model_kwargs' (customer attribution goes to merged_headers[LITELLM_CUSTOMER_ID_HEADER]), so in production the extra body is always {}. The factory tests mock _configure_direct_runtime_overrides and hand-write model_kwargs, passing against a contract production never produces.
findings.impact: Documented 'user' attribution never reaches LiteLLM, and a regression in the real header/budget injection for STT would fail no test.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the dead extra-body path and fix the docstring, or populate it deliberately. Add a test that runs the real _configure_direct_runtime_overrides (mocking only budget/DB lookups) and asserts the attribution STT actually sends (e.g. default_headers[LITELLM_CUSTOMER_ID_HEADER]).

findings.title: Phoenix usage written under non-OpenInference keys
findings.problem: update_current_generation writes usage as span attributes 'llm.usage.<key>' (audio_seconds, input, output, total). OpenInference token counts use 'llm.token_count.*', so Phoenix will not surface this usage as token counts. Also, when no recording span exists the method returns before update_current_observation, so input/output/metadata are skipped, unlike the exception path.
findings.impact: The story requires the same data (including usage) when Phoenix is active; usage will be missing or unrendered there. Reachability of the span-None branch was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Map usage to llm.token_count.prompt/completion/total (and a custom attribute for audio_seconds); decide whether the span-None case should still call update_current_observation; add a test for both.

findings.title: Broad except ValueError maps faults to 400
findings.problem: recognize_speech catches any ValueError from the whole call chain and returns it as HTTP 400 with str(e) in details and the hint 'Pick a model from GET /v1/audio_transcription_models'. JSONDecodeError, pydantic ValidationError and the AzureOpenAI missing-endpoint ValueError (get_stt_openai_client with empty STT_API_URL) are ValueError subclasses.
findings.impact: Server-side parse or config faults surface as client errors with internal messages and a misleading hint; real unknown-model errors are indistinguishable from them.
findings.recommendation: Raise a dedicated UnknownSttModelError from resolve_stt_model and catch only that in the router; let other errors map to 502/500.

findings.title: Trace name differs from acceptance criterion
findings.problem: Criterion: an STT request creates a Langfuse trace named 'speech-to-text' with a generation 'stt.transcribe'. Code sets TRACE_NAME = 'Audio Transcription' (applied via update_current_trace(name=TRACE_NAME)); 'speech-to-text' only appears as the metadata 'type'. The spec header calls this a known, agreed deviation and says the ticket will be updated, but the criterion text is unchanged.
findings.impact: A required criterion is unmet as written; dashboards or queries keyed on the criterion's trace name will not find these traces.
findings.recommendation: Human decision: either rename the trace to 'speech-to-text', or amend the ticket criterion to 'Audio Transcription' and record that in the story before merge.

findings.title: Header deny-lists miss hop-by-hop and CORS names
findings.problem: A configured '*' pattern still passes names outside the fixed deny-lists. Request side: accept-encoding, content-encoding, te, upgrade, keep-alive, expect, proxy-connection, api-key, x-forwarded-*. Response side (_UNSAFE_RESPONSE_HEADERS): location, www-authenticate, server, date, access-control-*. Response values override headers already set by middleware on the caller's response.
findings.impact: Only reachable when an admin configures a broad pattern (reachability of such configs unconfirmed), but then provider headers can override CodeMie CORS/auth response headers or break decoding on the upstream request.
findings.recommendation: Extend both deny-lists with these names and the access-control-* prefix, and add a test for a '*' pattern against them.

findings.title: New code misses Types And Imports standard
findings.problem: code-quality.md asks for parameterized generics, X | None, and explicit types on public functions. Violations in new code: select_forward_headers (stt_service.py:127) and _collect_response_headers (:134) return bare dict; _model_type_of (enterprise/litellm/models.py:225) takes bare dict with no return type; ConversationService.recognize_speech (conversation_service.py:1333) leaves file and the return unannotated; stt_config is Optional[SttConfig] (llm_config.py:255) and new LLMService STT methods use Optional[LLMModel]/Optional[str].
findings.impact: Documented project standard is not met, and the gates (ruff) do not enforce it.
findings.recommendation: Annotate as dict[str, str] / dict[str, Any] with an explicit ModelType return, file: BinaryIO and return SttResult (TYPE_CHECKING import), and use SttConfig | None, LLMModel | None, str | None.

findings.title: Unconfigured STT falls through to legacy client
findings.problem: When resolve_stt_model returns None (no STT_API_KEY, no LiteLLM audio model) the model is None and _build_client still builds the legacy AzureOpenAI client from empty STT_API_URL/STT_API_KEY. transcribe also ignores model_name when user is falsy.
findings.impact: A direct POST while stt_support is false produces an unstructured error (the AzureOpenAI ValueError is currently reported as 400 by CR-003) instead of a clean 503 'not configured'.
findings.recommendation: In transcribe/_build_client, raise ExtendedHTTPException 503 'Speech recognition is not configured' when no model resolves, and reject model_name with no user.

findings.title: Context passed to LiteLLM factory is unasserted
findings.problem: _build_client passes litellm_context, user_email and user_id from context vars to get_litellm_stt_client. Tests replace the factory with a fixed-return mock and no test inspects its call arguments; TestUserLiteLLMContext only asserts set_llm_context was called.
findings.impact: If the wrong model or context is passed, STT calls lose per-user budget and credential attribution while every current test still passes.
findings.recommendation: Assert litellm_factory.call_args (llm_model_details, litellm_context, user_email, user_id) against values placed in the context vars.
